doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Faculty connections and the no-jazz-on-Sunday dispute
summary: Only Frank Piano of the Romance Language department played with them; President McEwen banned Sunday jazz, they wrote a song and Dean Tolles settled it.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Did the Catatonic Five have any connection to the music department?

Not to the music department, but you might say, well, no. I was starting to think about the Alumni All-Stars, that was Paul Parker who was on the faculty for the art department but not the music department.

Well wait a minute. Frank Piano was a Spanish assistant professor here. And he used to come and play tenor with us now and then, the Catatonic Five. But that was the only connection we had with the faculty and the music department. He actually wasn’t in the music department, he was in the Romance Language department.
And what’s this business about — was it the president of the college at that time didn’t want no jazz on Sundays?

Sandy McEwen was a Presbyterian minister who, I don’t know it’d be very difficult to think of the things that he did like and approve of, but he certainly didn’t like us and approve of us, and he heard we were going to play a jazz session, I think it was at the Deke House. And he said, “No there’ll be no jazz on Sundays.” So we wrote a song called “Sandy Don’t ‘Low no Jazz on Sunday” you probably heard it. And it was a favorite of Ellie Wertimer’s. She would ask for that all the time. And in those days it was quite popular and we weathered the thing. We actually played it anyway. Dean Tolles was the moderator. He mediated the dispute by interpreting the president McEwen’s prohibition as being prohibition of music outside on a Sunday. So we moved it inside and
it was fine. Because he thought it would compete with chapel or something. Anyway. It had a happy ending.
